ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.

ops.oldText: Except as otherwise specified below, all actions, disputes, claims and controversies under common law, statutory law or in equity of any type or nature whatsoever,
ops.newText: All actions, disputes, claims and controversies under common law, statutory law or in equity of any type or nature whatsoever,

ops.oldText: (b) any previous or subsequent agreement between the parties; and/or (c) any other relationship, transaction or dealing between the parties (collectively the "Disputes"), will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com).
ops.newText: (b) any previous or subsequent agreement between the parties; and/or (c) any other relationship, transaction or dealing between the parties (collectively the "Disputes"), will be brought exclusively in the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved governing law from Arizona to the State of New York and replaced the USA&M arbitration mechanic with exclusive resolution in the state and federal courts in New York County, and deleted the "Except as otherwise specified below" opener so no competing dispute path survives. Delaware or California law and courts would be an acceptable fallback.
proposal.summary: New York law with all Disputes brought exclusively in the state and federal courts in New York County, and the competing carve-out opener removed.

mappings.element: Laws of the State of New York.
Exclusive jurisdiction of the state courts in New York County.
Exclusive jurisdiction of the federal courts in New York County.
